summary: This component displays blog articles filtered by a specific tag. It extracts the tag from the URL, looks up the human-readable tag name from the blog posts, filters posts matching that tag, and renders them in a card layout — or shows an appropriate message if no tag was specified or no posts were found.

explanations.14: This type says a Tag can be either a plain string or an object with a label property, since tags in the blog metadata might be stored in different formats.
explanations.18: matchPath checks if the current URL matches the pattern /blog/tags/:slug and extracts the slug parameter from it — it's how we know which tag the user wants to see.
explanations.22: We safely access the slug from the URL match; if the URL doesn't match our expected pattern, match will be undefined and rawTag will be undefined too.
explanations.42: This helper function normalizes any Tag into a string label — if it's already a string, use it as-is; if it's an object, pull out its label property.
explanations.45: We start by assuming the display tag is just the URL slug, but then search through posts to find the original, human-readable tag name that corresponds to this slug.
explanations.47: We're looking through the tags in each post to find one that, when converted to a slug, matches the slug from the URL — this lets us recover the original tag name.
explanations.59: For each post, we check if any of its tags match our target tag by comparing their slugs; this is how we know which posts to include in our filtered list.
explanations.61: We sort the filtered posts by date in descending order (newest first) by converting dates to milliseconds and subtracting in reverse — higher numbers come before lower numbers.
explanations.66: The translate function dynamically creates the page title by replacing {label} with the actual tag name, allowing different languages to format the title differently.
explanations.88: We construct the RSS feed URL by combining the base tag route with the slug and the rss.xml filename.
explanations.122: We pass getTagDisplayLabel (which maps the tag to its display name from the tags configuration) to the FollowFeed component so the feed label matches what users see in the feed itself.
